review: Reviewed Wren's round-329 request (Hand-lash a branch crossing with multiple wraps: a learnable bare-hand method for binding two owned branch pieces at a crossing with several wraps and a reversible closure, with measured fit and bounded hand-load trials; her single-wrap reed binding of two 31.6 mm pieces held 5 N separation and 1 N sliding for 10 s each and was untied, which establishes no structural capacity; actual owned pieces and cord of sufficient measured length, no tools, anchors or extra material, and her 0.54 m cord not assumed long enough; paid learning and work with preserved reservations, paid progress and an explicit cancellation contract; measuring, attempting, inspecting, bounded hand tests and untying with honest shortages, slip and damage, and no shelter, strength rating or wellbeing gain) and the World Agent's develop review (learning 5): a general parameterized Hand-lash crossing pieces with modes attempt, inspect, trial, untie and cancel; 2-4 adjacent turns, crossing angles 30-90 degrees, one continuous straight unknotted and unjoined cord or fragment and two owned untreated branch units; hand-bind-crossing@1 kept for single wraps; study 5 rounds at 0.2 energy; wrapCount + 3 paid rounds at 0.5 (measure-position, one routing round per turn, form-tuck-closure, dress-release-check); inspect 0.2; trial 0.5 with 0 < force <= 10 N and 0 < hold <= 60 s, separate or slide; untie one closure-release round plus one per turn at 0.5; free cancel; an explicit collision-free centreline per adjacent turn in the obtuse-bisector plane with transitions, finite width and one shared closure; the required length as the longest simultaneously occupied stage plus pinches and tails, not a multiplied single wrap; a paid measured shortfall that releases the unchanged inputs once; explicit contact paths and per-turn tension and slack before any released success or loaded trial, never equal load sharing or multiplied capacity; reuse of the crossing-contact@1, fiber-cord@1, cord-knot@1 and cord-bend@1 laws; conservation, pause, resume, cancel, death, wear once per cord and no reward, shelter, hanging load or rating. The specification is self-consistent and every gated physical transition has an explicit rule, so this is a simplified real mechanism, not a first release. Implemented hand-lash-crossing@1 in scope long-ex16 (new module packages/world-core/src/long-crossing-lashing.ts, export LONG_CROSSING_LASHING, handler long.hand-lash-crossing, events prefixed crossing-lashing-, law multi-turn-contact@1, method adjacent-turns-overhand-closure, item processing key crossingLashing), registered at the end of V7_PACKAGES with package dependencies foundation-open@1, hand-twist-fiber-cord@1, hand-tie-cord-knot@1, hand-join-fiber-cords@1 and hand-bind-crossing@1; learning 5 with learningEnergy 0.2, each study round paid; no prerequisite; references are empty, so all ids are exact; the ability serializes to 3,449 code units within the 3,500 limit. Modes and costs: attempt (pieceIds: two own untreated branch items of one whole unit each, the first on top, where a two-unit lot may be named twice and gives up one unit as a new conserved item with its source recorded; cordId; crossingAngle; integer wrapCount 2-4) reserves the three items and pays wrapCount + 3 rounds of 0.5 energy through workPay, continuing each round and resumable only by attempt with workId; a loose tucked lashing left by cancellation or creep needs only the dressing round; inspect (bindingId or workId) costs 0.2 and changes nothing; trial (bindingId, trialForce, trialDuration, trialDirection) costs 0.5; untie pays wrapCount + 1 rounds of 0.5 (withdraw-closure-end, then unwrap-turn-n down to unwrap-turn-1); cancel is free. Every validation (mastery, arguments, exact own ids, rigid-piece, strand and friction laws, whole untreated sound pieces, a straight two-ply cord of at least 0.2 unit that is not knotted, joined, bound or reserved, a material-independent least length for that width and turn count, footing, the work circle, clear dry ground for the crossed 2 m pieces, energy and no unfinished own work) precedes any charge, so refusals spend nothing; no material is consumed. Modeling assumptions of multi-turn-contact@1: piece measurement, cord width and bend limit, crossing pose and layout, hand span, lift, room, closure, pinch, tail, grip-site and bending rules are crossing-contact@1's, called through a new append-only CROSSING_CONTACT export; adjacent turns lie in planes parallel to the obtuse-bisector plane, symmetric about the middle and one cord width apart measured square to the helical cord (pitch w / sqrt(1 - (w/P)^2)); shifting the plane by d moves the top section by d tan(angle/2) along the bisector and the bottom section the other way; each turn's planar centreline is the convex hull of both elliptical sections offset by w/2, traced by 720 support points (collision-free by construction; the middle turn reproduces crossing-contact@1's wrap within 0.5 mm) and its length adds a helical advance of one pitch (hypot of hull length and pitch); each turn starts and ends at the top piece's crown; the ends leave the outer turns' crowns, n x pitch / sin(beta) apart along the top piece, and ride one width up onto the turns to one overhand closure over the middle (hypot(n pitch / (2 sin beta), w) per end), formed and seated by the crossing-contact@1 and cord-knot@1 closure, opening, curvature, pinch and tail rules and counted once; while a turn is passed under the lifted crossing only that turn carries the 0.04 m fingertip allowance, the earlier turns being pinned on the hull by the holding hand, so from the second turn the held thickness is the stack plus 2w within the 0.1 m one-hand span; the required length is the maximum over every routing stage and the forming stage plus 2 x 0.02 m pinch and the seated stage plus two 0.02 m + w tails; on the paused round-329 state Wren's actual 0.54 m, 6.4 mm cord item-303-wren-3473 on her two 31.6 mm pieces needs 0.6273 m for two turns at 90 degrees and 0.5818 m at 30 degrees, a paid measured shortfall that releases her items unchanged, while a 0.64 m cord made by hand-twist-sectioned-cord@1 fits two turns (0.6124 m at 90 degrees) and no hand-twisted cord fits three; hand-held turns relax on interruption (all routed turns fall loose and are routed again in further paid rounds, a moved layout is laid again, prior expenditure is kept), and an opened untie falls open; dressing pulls both ends with cord-bend@1's 5 N and, sliding inward over the bark, the tension falls by the Coulomb capstan relation dT = 0.3 T d(theta) over each turn's actual bark contact (crossing-contact@1's 0.3 reed on bark times the hull's turning angles and its bridging share), each point keeping the tension from its nearer end, so the outer turns of a real two-turn lashing carry about 3.4 and 1.4 N on their two sides and inner turns far less; this integrates the same friction law that crossing-contact@1 linearizes for one uniform 5 N wrap, so a single turn computed here would hold less in slide, one more reason single wraps stay with hand-bind-crossing@1; the release check needs the closure's cord-bend@1 slip load above 5 N and tails of 0.02 m + w; a trial puts one hand on each piece at crossing-contact@1's grip site moved out by half the band of turns, with force = min(trialForce, 200 N x health/100, 10000 N/m x the narrower piece); separate is resisted first by the turns' side tensions times their inclination and then by each turn stretching under the fiber-cord@1 stiffness over its own length, slack turns only after their slack is taken up, against closure slip at the end tensions and the curvature-adjusted breaking force at the peak tension; slide slips at 0.3 times the integrated tension of every turn over its top-piece contact, so slack or low-tension turns contribute only their actual contact (a real two-turn lashing slips at about 4.3 N; on one 4.3 mm fixture cord two, three and four turns slip at 4.5, 4.9 and 4.9 N), and a crossing slip migrates every turn one width; axial and circumferential friction are taken independently, and cord-on-cord friction between turns and under the ends is not represented, which understates holding; strand damage above half the breaking force, piece bending and fragments follow crossing-contact@1 and fiber-cord@1; creep under a held trial is fiber-cord@1's law per turn at its mean tension, lengthening the cord at constant volume and lowering that turn's tension uniformly, and a lashing whose turns are all slack is loose; static lashings do not creep, as in crossing-contact@1; between rounds a cord that can no longer carry its own peak tension parts where the more loaded end enters its outer turn into two owned fragments of conserved length and quantity; a retained lashing is carried as owned items holding both pieces, so no hanging load acts; the cord takes the bound role while tucked or bound, so hand-bind-crossing@1's existing bound-role wear of 0.0005 per round applies exactly once and fiber-cord@1's own wear applies while it is a cord; all three items are reserved for the lashing id, so transfers, knots, joins, single-wrap bindings and straight trials are refused; joined cord is refused as unrepresented; untie needs condition 0.5 and the existing jam rule; death stops the work, leaves the items where the person died once and keeps a tucked or bound relation; released undamaged pieces keep no record. Events crossing-lashing-started, -measured, -shortfall, -turn-routed, -closure-formed, -release-held, -release-failed, -relaxed, -paused, -resumed, -cancelled, -stopped, -inspected, -trial, -grip-slipped, -crossing-slipped, -closure-slipped, -damaged, -broken, -loosened, -resisted, -closure-withdrawn, -turn-unwrapped and -untied are emitted only when they occur and carry reusable schematic view metadata (component crossing-lashing reusing the crossing-binding, fiber-cord and cord-knot views with recorded provenance: actor, work and lashing ids, exact items, crossing angle and pose, turn count, per-turn offset, length, 13-point routed centreline, pinned, loose, snug or slack state, slack and migration, bridges, closure and tails, condition, grip sites, retention and evidence event ids; only routed turns are drawn and a completed appearance follows only the passed release check); visualComponents is empty. Inspection reports visible state only and keeps turn tensions and holding force unknown. Bounded verified findings use the existing personal records keyed by the functional observation and turn count (lashing-fit, lashing-hand-load-separate or -slide, lashing-untie), so repeated identical trials are no new information and single-wrap facts are not duplicated; release-held carries no qualified flag, so no milestone, pleasure, satisfaction or comfort follows, and no reward, shelter effect or strength rating is added. Reuse: hand-bind-crossing@1 through the appended CROSSING_CONTACT export (its ability text and behavior unchanged), hand-twist-fiber-cord@1 through FIBER_CORD, hand-tie-cord-knot@1 through CORD_KNOT and hand-join-fiber-cords@1 through CORD_BEND; cords made by hand-twist-sectioned-cord@1 are ordinary cords; all reused abilities stay byte-identical. Tests in apps/simulator/test/long-ex16-hand-lash-crossing.test.ts cover scope, dependencies and byte-identical reused abilities, the size limit and wording, the five paid study rounds, the paid measured shortfall of a real cord of Wren's 0.54 m size on real gathered branch units, the explicit turn geometry and longest-stage need, pre-cost refusals, the five paid rounds with a real 0.64 m sectioned cord, separate and slide trials with per-turn tensions, a four-turn fixture cord lengthened in place with conserved volume (no hand-twisted cord fits four turns) with inner turns carrying less and a slack turn contributing nothing, damage and breaking, untying and resistance, pause, relaxation, resume, cancel and loose dressing, inspection, single wear, owner-only rules and death.
